sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 just before its planned IPO roadshow, pairing benchmark gains with a 20% price cut. The day's broader theme is competition moving from raw model capability to agent harnesses and distribution channels.

sections.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of IPO
sections.content: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, two models built on the same underlying model but split by safeguards: Fable 5.2 is open to all users with biology and cybersecurity guardrails, while Mythos 5.2 is limited to vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. Anthropic reported gains in coding, science, chart understanding and robotics benchmarks, cited a prototype operating system built by 1,000+ sub-agents over eight days, and cut standard pricing to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, 20% below the prior generation. Coverage ties the release to Anthropic's planned IPO.
sections.significance: The strongest single event of the day: a flagship frontier release that also resets Anthropic's price point and is explicitly framed as positioning ahead of a public listing.
sections.transition_hint: Anthropic's release leans on agent orchestration; DeepSeek's numbers show that layer becoming a standalone battleground.

sections.title: DeepSeek Harness reaches 1.54 million daily active users
sections.content: DeepSeek disclosed on X that its open-source agent application DeepSeek Harness reached 1.54 million daily active users by Nov 4, less than three months after its Aug 13 debut, up from about 271,000 at the end of September after a desktop client launched. Reports describe Harness as model-agnostic, able to connect to Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM or any compatible model service, and say DeepSeek plans an official plugin marketplace plus a support program for plugin creators.
sections.significance: A concrete adoption milestone that positions DeepSeek in the agent-harness layer rather than only model performance, directly challenging Claude Code and Codex-style products.
sections.transition_hint: If harnesses are the new front line, model access through developer platforms is the distribution channel that feeds them.

sections.title: Vercel adds Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash to Token Pass
sections.content: Vercel announced that GLM 5.3 Flash, Z.ai's multimodal coding model with a 1M-token context window, is now available in Token Pass, a $30/month Pro-team subscription granting $80 in monthly credit through AI Gateway. The model is listed alongside Kimi K3, GLM 5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, supports text and image inputs, function calling, structured output and streaming, and is available as zai/glm-5.3-flash with zero data retention by default.
sections.significance: A concrete distribution win for a Chinese open-weight model family inside a major developer platform, and evidence that coding-agent subscriptions are becoming a packaging layer for model access.
sections.transition_hint: Platform packaging matters more when the underlying spend is concentrated; a new survey quantifies just how concentrated it is.

sections.title: Menlo Ventures report: Chinese models take 89% of open-source enterprise spend
sections.content: A Menlo Ventures report, based on a September survey of nearly 400 US enterprise decision-makers, says Chinese models account for 89% of global enterprise spending on open-source models: Moonshot's Kimi at 61%, DeepSeek at 15%, Z.ai's GLM at 11% and Meta's Llama at 7%. The report also says open-source models are only 4% of overall model spend, while Anthropic and OpenAI together hold 86% of API spend.
sections.significance: The clearest quantitative snapshot of where open-weight enterprise money sits, and a contrast with the closed-API dominance that Anthropic's launch is competing within.
sections.transition_hint: Spend share is one lens; enterprise distribution deals are another way vendors reach buyers.

sections.title: ChatGPT Enterprise goes live on AWS Marketplace
sections.content: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT Enterprise is now available on AWS Marketplace, per a Sina Finance flash report.
sections.significance: A procurement-channel move that puts OpenAI's enterprise product inside cloud marketplace billing, though the supplied signal is a single short flash with no terms or figures.
sections.transition_hint: Enterprise channels are one route to buyers; infrastructure capital commitments are another, at a very different scale.

sections.title: SoftBank, Grab and PETROS sign JDA for $1.85B Malaysia AI infrastructure
sections.content: SoftBank Group, Grab and Petroleum Sarawak Berhad signed joint development agreements for $1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital to build AI infrastructure in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of five gigawatts or more of AI compute capacity. The initial capital comprises $1 billion from SoftBank, $750 million from Grab and $100 million from PETROS, deployed in stages subject to development and customer-contract milestones; the parties will seek additional investors and hyperscaler customers.
sections.significance: A large regional compute commitment that shows AI infrastructure buildout spreading beyond US and Chinese hubs, though it involves none of the named AI model organizations.

sections.title: Cross-Org Themes
content: Agent harnesses and coding-agent packaging are becoming a distinct competitive layer, spanning Anthropic's multi-agent orchestration claims, DeepSeek Harness adoption and Vercel's Token Pass bundling
Price and access terms are shifting: Anthropic cut flagship pricing 20% while gating its most capable variant, and GLM 5.3 Flash arrives through a low-cost subscription tier

sections.title: Rumors and Unverified Claims
sections.content: OpenAI is reportedly developing a ChatGPT business-mention tracking dashboard that would let brands claim their business and monitor mentions and clicks; the report is based on a LinkedIn screenshot and unnamed sources and describes the tool as close to launching, not launched.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The competitive question this week is less which model tops a benchmark than who controls the harness, the subscription and the procurement channel through which models reach users. Next evidence to watch: whether Anthropic's price cut and Mythos access expansion translate into enterprise spend, and whether DeepSeek's Harness growth converts into its planned plugin marketplace.
